item.title: Mozu Tombs: The Giant Keyhole Kofun of Sakai — Guide
item.description: The Mozu Tombs in Sakai are a group of giant burial mounds built in the fifth century for the rulers of early Japan, inscribed together with the nearby Furuichi group as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The greatest of them, the Daisen Kofun, is traditionally attributed to Emperor Nintoku: a keyhole-shaped mound 486 metres long, ringed by moats, its scale rivalling the Great Pyramid and the tomb of the First Emperor of China.
